title: Quantum Reserve: Headroom Leasing, Burst Escrow, and Tenant Safety Budgets PRD
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: PRD for the Quantum Reserve experiment: a new reserved capacity primitive that combines fractional reservation units (quantums), a headroom leasing model for autoscale buffer, and a burst escrow system backed by tenant safety budgets. Goal is to reduce cold-starts and soft-failures on Dedicated while preserving strong tenant isolation and predictable unit economics.
background: Customers ask for predictable latency at lower cost than always-on capacity. Current reserved pools are coarse-grained and either over-provision or lead to hard throttles during transient spikes. Previous PRDs cover proportional reserves, soft-evict, and burst policies; this spec introduces a composable primitive that can be layered on top of existing reservoirs to provide elastic, accountable burst without sacrificing isolation guarantees.
problem_statement: Engineering teams need a way to allow tenants to temporarily exceed their committed throughput with transparent accounting and automatic graceful degradation. Existing approaches either allow uncontrolled borrowing (risking noisy neighbor effects) or rigid caps (causing customer-visible failures). We need a mechanism that: 1) enables fractional reserved units to reduce wasted capacity, 2) provides a pre-authorized headroom buffer that autoscaler can lease dynamically, and 3) enforces burst escrow debits tied to a tenant safety budget that decays predictably.
goals: Introduce 'quantum reserves' allowing tenants to reserve fractional capacity units (min quantum = 0.01 GPU-slot) to improve utilization.
Implement headroom leasing: short-lived leased capacity that autoscaler can request for burst handling and warmup pre-warming.
Design a burst escrow accounting model where bursts consume escrow credits that replenish on a defined cadence or via purchases.
Provide tenant safety budgets and hard isolation fallbacks: if safety budget exhausted, fallback to a defined degradation policy rather than impacting other tenants.
Deliver Console controls and APIs to configure quantums, lease parameters, and escrow policies with clear billing implications.
Ensure observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-tenant escrow usage timeseries, and SLO degradation alerts.
non_goals: Full marketplace for buying arbitrary extra capacity (this PRD only defines primitive and billing model).
Replacing all existing reserve UIs; we will add new controls and keep legacy flows for migration.
Changing core runtime kernel selection for quantized models (implementation should work with current runtime hooks).
user_stories: As an SRE for AcmeCorp, I want my reserved capacity to incur less waste by allowing 0.1 quantum reservations so I can reduce cost while keeping latency targets.
As a Platform Owner, I want a small pre-warmed headroom lease that can be grabbed during minute-long spikes to avoid cold KV-cache misses.
As an Operator, I want burst escrow usage visible in billing and the ability to set a safety budget threshold that triggers conservative degradation instead of evicting other tenants.
As a DevRel customer, I want to be able to simulate burst exhaustion in test environments to validate fallback behavior before going to production.
As a Console user, I want a simple toggle to enable quantum reserves and to specify lease TTLs and escrow replenishment cadence.
requirements: API: POST /v1/dedicated/reserves to support decimal 'quantum_size' and 'min_quantum' fields.
API: New endpoint POST /v1/dedicated/headroom/lease for autoscaler to request short-lived leases: params {tenant_id, desired_quantums, ttl_seconds, purpose_tag}.
Runtime: Leases must be enforceable by scheduler within 500ms of approval and pre-warm hooks should trigger KV-cache prefetch for leased slots.
Billing: Escrow accounting must capture per-lease debit, show current escrow balance, and tie to monthly invoice line items with a clear conversion (quantum-hours -> dollars).
Console: Dedicated UI in Tenant -> Capacity showing quantum reservations, escrow balance, lease history, and a 'Safety budget' slider with recommended defaults.
Policy: Safety budget configurations support three modes: soft (best-effort), conservative (prefer degradation), strict (block bursts when below threshold).
Observability: Telemetry exported to internal metrics pipeline: reserve_quantums_allocated_gauge, headroom_lease_requests_total, escrow_debits_total, safety_budget_remaining_gauge.
Acceptance tests: end-to-end test simulating spike traffic must demonstrate reduced P95 latency regression compared to baseline with no leases for 80% of spikes under 60s.
Migration: import tool to convert existing coarse reservations into quantum buckets with recommended mapping and expected billing delta report.
Security: RBAC controls to limit who can modify safety budgets and escrow purchase permissions; changes logged in audit trail.
Docs: Public PRD + API reference and console walkthrough published before GA.
Compliance: Ensure AML and audit logs record headroom lease approvals and escrow purchases for enterprise customers.
Rollback: Feature flag gating by org; must be reversible without data loss within 24 hours.
acceptance_criteria: API endpoints implemented and covered by contract tests; swagger spec updated and published.
Autoscaler can acquire and release headroom leases reliably within 500ms in integration runs on staging clusters.
Telemetry shows escrow_debits_total increments for each lease and escrow balances reconcile with simulated billing invoices within 1% error over 72 hours.
Console surfaces : quantum reservation table, escrow balance, and safety budget slider; UI tests validate state transitions.
E2E spike test: 100 synthetic tenants generate randomized bursts; 95th percentile request latency does not exceed baseline SLA by more than 20% for tenants with active leases.
Safety budget 'conservative' mode triggers degradation policy (e.g., lossy sampling / priority-queueing) before cross-tenant preemption in >99% of tests where budget is below threshold.
Migration tool produces mapping report for at least five customer demo accounts and provides estimated monthly bill delta.
Feature flag per-org works: enable/disable toggles take effect immediately and no leaked leases remain after disablement.
Security: audit log entries created for all lease grants and escrow top-ups and visible in tenant audit view.
Documentation: public API docs, console guide, and a one-page billing explainer published and linked from Console within GA rollout.
success_metrics: Reduce wasted reserved capacity (measured as idle-quantum-hours / reserved-quantum-hours) by >= 18% for pilot tenants within first 30 days.
Decrease tenant-visible cold-start latency incidents by >= 40% during transient spikes for tenants using headroom leases.
Adoption: 25% of tenants on Dedicated with >1k q-requests/day enable quantum reserve within first quarter after GA.
Escrow revenue: optional escrow purchases account for measurable incremental ARR within 90 days for enterprise pilots.
Operational: No increase in cross-tenant SLO violations attributable to leases after 60 days of rollout.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal alpha (engineering + 3 pilot tenants) behind org feature flag and manual escrow ledger. Phase 2: Closed beta with billing integration and console controls for 10 customers. Phase 3: GA with full billing, RBAC, and migration tool. Each phase includes a 2-week soak period and a rollback window. Telemetry and billing reconciliation must pass before progressing to the next phase.
monitoring_and_alerting: Create dashboards: Headroom Lease QPS, Escrow Debit Rate, Safety Budget Exhaustion Count, Cross-tenant Preemptions. Alert: safety_budget_exhaustion_rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m -> paging to infra-oncall. Billing reconciliation anomalies (>5% delta) -> pager for finance-eng.
dependencies: Scheduler autoscale hooks (ENG-331210) must be extended to call headroom lease API.
Billing pipeline changes to accept quantum-hour line items (FIN-2026-qhrs).
Console front-end capacity component (DES-16034) for new UI surfaces.
Telemetry exporter update to include new metrics (ENG-339900).
Migration tool library (PM-847000) to map legacy reservations into quantums.
Legal review for escrow/billing model and TOS update (LEGAL-92).
risks: Noisy neighbor risk if lease enforcement lags scheduler; mitigated with strict headroom TTL and automatic revoke on contention.
Billing complexity increases leading to customer confusion; mitigated by a simple billing explainer and dashboard projection tool.
Overly aggressive quantum defaults could fragment allocation and increase scheduler overhead; mitigated with conservative default quantum sizes and autoscaling thresholds.
Cross-region edge cases where lease approvals in one zone cannot be honored in another; mitigation: zone-local leases only and clear console warning.
Regulatory risk for escrow funds in certain countries; mitigation: restrict escrow purchases by jurisdiction at GA.

notes: Prefer conservative launch defaults: min_quantum = 0.05, default safety_budget = 10 quantum-hours/month. Pilot customers should be auto-invited and given a billing credit to exercise escrow purchases. Follow-up epics may include marketplace purchase flow and per-route quantum tagging.
